title: ISRO's Impossible Space Economics: How India Landed on the Moon's South Pole for ₹615 Crore

scenes.voiceoverText: In 1963, Indian scientists carried their first rocket nosecone to a Kerala beach on a bicycle.
scenes.captionMarkup: In *1963,* Indian scientists carried their first *rocket nosecone* to a Kerala beach on a *bicycle.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Sixty years later, India became the first nation to land on the Moon's South Pole! Stay with me — one locked number explains why superpowers now ride Indian rockets.
scenes.beatACaption: Sixty years later, India became the *first nation* to land on the *Moon's South Pole!*
scenes.beatBCaption: Stay with me — *one locked number* explains why superpowers now *ride Indian rockets.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Hollywood spent ₹1,350 crore just to film Interstellar — while Russia's Luna-25 crashed days earlier.
scenes.captionMarkup: Hollywood spent *₹1,350 crore* just to film *Interstellar* — while *Luna-25* crashed days earlier.

scenes.voiceoverText: Yet ISRO built, launched, and landed Chandrayaan-3 on the actual Moon for just ₹615 crore!
scenes.captionMarkup: Yet *ISRO* built, launched, and landed *Chandrayaan-3* on the actual Moon for just *₹615 crore!*

scenes.voiceoverText: How? Five Earth-orbit slingshots that save massive fuel — plus 90% homegrown parts from 400 Indian firms!
scenes.captionMarkup: How? *Five Earth-orbit slingshots* that save fuel — plus *90% homegrown* parts from *400 Indian firms!*

scenes.voiceoverText: When foreign powers denied India cryogenic engines, ISRO engineered its own CE-20 stage and laser-guided Vikram lander.
scenes.captionMarkup: Denied *cryogenic tech,* ISRO built its own *CE-20 engine* and laser-guided *Vikram lander.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Unlocked: Sriharikota has launched 434 foreign satellites for 36 countries — including 104 on one single rocket!
scenes.captionMarkup: Unlocked: *434 foreign satellites* launched for *36 countries* — including *104 on one rocket!*

scenes.voiceoverText: From the UK and Singapore to over 230 satellites for America — the world queues up at ISRO!
scenes.captionMarkup: From the *UK* and *Singapore* to *230+ satellites* for *America* — the world queues at *ISRO!*

scenes.voiceoverText: Now, the honest part: India still holds just 2% of the global space market and lacks reusable boosters.
scenes.captionMarkup: Now, the *honest* part: India holds just *2%* of the global space market and lacks *reusable boosters.*

scenes.voiceoverText: That is why Gaganyaan, reusable Soorya rockets, and 300 space startups are scaling right now. A country that rents orbit is a passenger. A country that launches the world is a navigator.
scenes.beatACaption: That is why *Gaganyaan,* reusable *Soorya rockets,* and *300+ startups* are scaling right now.
scenes.beatBCaption: A country that rents orbit is a *passenger.* A country that launches the world is a *navigator.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Which mission makes you proudest — Chandrayaan-3, Mangalyaan, or Gaganyaan? One word below.
